cross_surface_assertions.title: Intentional Chrome active-tab capture
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: The extension reads only the user-invoked active tab, shows a reviewable preview, and sends nothing until the user presses an explicit Submit control.
evidence_requirements: recording shows no network submission before Submit
capture trace records activeTab permission and the visible tab URL/title without browsing history
submitted payload identifies TS-CORE-01 and a synthetic-data label
backend audit records one user-initiated submission
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: One deliberate invocation plus one explicit Submit creates one scoped synthetic capture; background tabs, history, and pre-submit network logs contain no capture.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Local simulated login
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: A clearly labeled local-only simulated account establishes account-a and never falls through to a real OAuth provider or production identity.
evidence_requirements: login screen and session trace say Local simulation or Demo
session contains stable account-a scope
network trace contains no Google, Apple, or production authentication request
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: Web and iOS authenticate to localhost as account-a using only the declared simulator and show the same account scope.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Account-scoped canonical persistence
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: Submitted evidence, proposed assertions, confirmations, actions, and outcomes persist under an immutable account scope in the shared backend.
evidence_requirements: before-and-after datastore trace names account-a, episode ID, candidate/assignment scope, and version
restart or second-client readback returns the persisted version
account-b retrieval is denied and discloses no object existence
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: Only account-a can read the persisted TS-CORE-01 episode and its version survives a backend restart or a new client session.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Web and iOS confirmed-state parity
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: Web and iOS render the same backend-owned confirmed fact version, values, evidence message IDs, status, and assignment scope.
evidence_requirements: Web readback JSON and screenshot
iOS readback JSON and screenshot
canonical backend snapshot
machine comparison of state ID, state version, assertion values, and evidence IDs
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: The machine comparison is exact and both clients make proposed versus confirmed state visibly distinct.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Fact confirmation is not action approval
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: Confirming selected facts creates confirmed state but no effect authority; the later action preview requires a separate current decision.
evidence_requirements: fact-confirmation event has its own event ID and scope
action proposal remains unapproved after fact confirmation
action-approval event has a different event ID, proposal version, exact target, and exact effect
declining action leaves confirmed facts intact
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: No effect row or destination result exists after fact confirmation alone; only a separate approval of the current preview can authorize the local effect.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Idempotent local effect with observed readback
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: The approved local-only effect uses one idempotency key and is called twice to simulate retry; both attempts resolve to one destination object whose fields are read back.
evidence_requirements: two execution attempts share one idempotency key
destination contains exactly one local effect object
both responses reconcile to the same external object ID
observed readback matches target and effect before success is shown
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: Exactly one local destination object exists and the UI reports verified only after matching readback.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Failure, revocation, deletion, and denial matrix
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: Offline, timeout, permission revocation, deletion, and cross-account access each fail safely without false success, duplicate effects, lost review state, or data leakage.
evidence_requirements: one deterministic trace per required variant
preserved or explicitly discarded user state is named
timeout reconciles before retry can duplicate
revocation blocks execution at use time
deletion removes registered derivatives and revokes retrieval first
account-b receives the same denial for absent and account-a-owned IDs
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: All five variants pass their exact checks; any unrun variant remains an explicit release gap.

cross_surface_assertions.title: Fixture and demo labeling
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: Every visible fixture, login, candidate record, action, destination, and result is labeled Demo, Fixture, Synthetic, Simulated, or Local-only at the point where it could be mistaken for live state.
evidence_requirements: one visible-state screenshot or output per review object
backend records carry synthetic classification
simulated results never use production-success language
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: A reviewer can identify the non-live boundary from every review object without relying on a separate README.

cross_surface_assertions.title: No live candidate data or live external writes
cross_surface_assertions.behavior: The entire run uses only the checked-in synthetic fixture and local destinations; no production credential, candidate source, telemetry sink, model provider, or external connector is contacted.
evidence_requirements: run manifests declare synthetic_fixture_only and contains_live_candidate_data false
credential inventory contains only local disposable values
network allowlist contains localhost only
artifact scan contains no raw candidate screenshot or unredacted production payload
cross_surface_assertions.pass_condition: All manifests and network evidence prove localhost-only operation and the artifact scan finds no live candidate data.

ts_core_01_evidence.pass_condition: All required artifacts resolve to one frozen commit set and trace ID; Web, iOS, and backend state keys match; confirmation and approval event IDs differ; two effect attempts reconcile to one observed local object; every recovery variant passes.
